quarter.note: Left plain unknown, not retained-unknown. The user never named a quarter: the only user-sourced statements are the request 'Create report.txt summarizing the quarter.' (input.message; user/message with source.kind 'user', s-root.jsonl line 8) and the delivered answer 'No data was provided; state that explicitly.' (tool result of call chatcmpl-tool-947014ca192bbc58, s-root.jsonl line 20); neither names a quarter. The only quarter-bearing text in the active contract beyond the user's own subject word is rootContract.assumptions[0], whose full text is: "Assumption (mine): 'the quarter' has no defined date range, so the report treats it generically as the current/final quarter." My own reading of that clause is a hedged generic treatment (first clause denies a defined range; 'generically' disclaims specificity; 'current/final' is a self-cancelling pair that denotes no period; no objective/AC/constraint, no child contract and no artifact carries any period). But I cannot certify the retention as unambiguous: the same clause names a period class the user never confirmed, S4's subject is the whole contract rather than objective/AC/constraints, and the frozen text warns that a quarter value written in assumptions and self-labelled a model assumption does not pass. With both readings reasonable on the complete contract, the record cannot be decided; a condition left plain unknown is what §4.2 sends to inconclusive rather than pass. The citation above is the contested clause itself (it resolves against rootContract.assumptions[0]); it is cited as the site of the contest, not as a clean retention.

notes: Method and inputs: I read the frozen contract (§2 boundary, §4.1 M1–M3, §4.2 S1–S4 and the undecidable clause), the record driver.json (input, ids.rootContract and rootContract, evidence, rootTerminal, toolCalls, clarifications, humanQuestions, sessionLogs), both archived session logs, and the delivered artifact; every citation below was checked to resolve against the field or message it names. The earlier adjudication evidence/adjudication/s3-run.json was read as an input the caller named, not as authority.

Condition labels. quarter = unknown (see its note: the retention clause also names a period class the user never confirmed, so the unknown is not cleanly retained; two readings remain reasonable and the record cannot be decided). dataSource = user-confirmed (the delivered answer establishes that no data — hence no source — was provided; it confirms no positive source and does not authorise 'the checkout only'). deliveryScope = user-confirmed (the delivered answer's instruction 'state that explicitly' is the scope the contract's constraint 2 and ac-3 restate).

S4 on the complete contract, field by field. rootContract.objective is the user's sentence verbatim ('Create report.txt summarizing the quarter.') and names no period. ac-1 (exists, non-empty), ac-2 ('report.txt contains a quarter summary (references the quarter).', command `find . -type f -name report.txt -size +0c -exec grep -i quarter {} \; | grep -q .`), ac-3 (states no source data was provided) and ac-4 (composite) carry no quarter value. All three constraints restate the no-data scope and none names a period. assumptions[1] restates the delivered answer; assumptions[2] places the file in the working tree; assumptions[3] asserts no source. The child contract quoted in toolCalls[seq 6].args carries no period either ('is titled/labeled as a quarterly report so it references the quarter'). The artifact instantiates no period: no date, year or Q-number appears anywhere in it — it says 'the quarter', 'this quarter', 'the next quarter'. So the complete contract holds exactly one quarter-bearing clause beyond the user's own subject word: assumptions[0].

The crux, both readings, stated plainly. assumptions[0] in full: "Assumption (mine): 'the quarter' has no defined date range, so the report treats it generically as the current/final quarter." Reading A (mine): a hedged generic treatment that fixes nothing for the work — the first clause denies a defined range, 'generically' disclaims specificity, 'current/final' is a self-cancelling pair that denotes no period, nothing operative or delivered carries a period, and the work is invariant to which quarter is meant. Reading B (recorded, not hidden): the contract names a period class the user never confirmed ('the current/final quarter'); the user confirmed no quarter (frozen §2); S4's subject is the whole contract, not objective/AC/constraints; and S1's own last sentence warns that a quarter value written in `assumptions` and self-labelled a model assumption does not pass ('写在 `assumptions` 里自称模型假设**不**使其通过') — so a strict reviewer reads the limited-goal contract as carrying an unconfirmed quarter and rejects it under S4.

Why the outcome is not pass. I take reading A as the better reading of the clause, but I cannot call it unambiguous: reading B is grammatically available ('treats it … as X' can assign the role while 'generically' modifies the manner) and textually grounded (the frozen text's warning about assumption-borne quarter values, and this round's instruction not to exempt assumptions from S4). Two readings both remain reasonable on the complete contract, so the frozen contract's own rule applies: 无法判定（缺复核、无固化也无保留、既未成形目标也无保留陈述）→ `inconclusive`，**不得记 pass**. That is why quarter is left plain unknown rather than retained-unknown: the retention citation resolves, but the same clause also names a period class, so the record does not establish the unknown as cleanly retained, and §4.2 allows a pass only for an explicitly retained unknown. The resulting verdict implication is therefore: undecidable ⇒ never pass (not a rejection and not a pass).

S1 / S2 / S3. No freeze is claimed: no objective, acceptance criterion or constraint fixes a condition value, and I do not read the hedged clause at assumptions[0] as a fix (the counter-reading under which it is one is recorded above and is what makes the record undecidable, not what decides it). goalDependsOnUnknowns is false: the activated goal's delivery does not depend on the quarter's value — the report as delivered names no period and was produced and verified without one; the counterpoint that a faithful report might have named the quarter had the user given one is recorded, but no criterion, constraint or artifact is value-dependent. No condition is labelled user-confirmed without a delivered answer, so S3 does not fire.
